title: ALP SoM preset (metadata/e1m_modules/<SKU>.yaml) v1
description: Schema for the per-SKU SoM preset.  The SDK's loader resolves the customer's board.yaml `som.sku` to the matching preset here.  Every released-MPN preset shares ONE canonical shape: the top-level key set, `memory:`, `on_module:`, `inference:`, and `status:` are closed (additionalProperties: false) so cross-family key drift fails validation instead of passing silently.  The only deliberately-open spots are the ones where genuine per-family variance is legitimate, and each carries its own description saying why: `capabilities:` (open set of accelerator flags matched against each library's `integration.zephyr.hw_backends:` block in metadata/libraries/*.yaml), `i2c_devices` bus KEYS (bus identifiers differ per family), and `helper_firmware[].flash_args` (shape follows the flash backend).

silicon_variant.description: SoC variant order code matching the vendor's datasheet (e.g. `AE302F80F55D5LE` for Alif E3, `R9A09G056N44GBG` for Renesas RZ/V2N, `MIMX9352xxxxM` for NXP i.MX 93 — the latter is partial pending the HW config writeup, encoded as `silicon_variant: TBD` per the project's no-inventing-values rule). Enables forward lookup of per-variant memory, optional features, and package-specific GPIO counts without reverse-scanning all SoC JSON files. Optional; when absent the loader falls back to reverse lookup via `alp_module_skus` in the SoC JSON.

on_module.description: Populated on-module chips + I2C bus topology.  The key set is CLOSED: every legal on-module role is enumerated below (union of all released families), so a new family inventing a synonym key (e.g. `pmic` for `pmic_main`) fails validation.  Adding a genuinely new on-module role means extending this enumeration deliberately, in the schema, with review.

silicon.description: Main silicon triple ref -- repeats the top-level `silicon:` for self-contained reads of the block.

pmic_main.description: Primary PMIC.  Canonical key on every family that populates one (imx93's former `pmic:` normalised to this).

pmic_secondary.description: Secondary PMIC (e.g. V2N's DA9292).  Absent on single-PMIC families.

supervisor_mcu.description: On-module supervisor / IO MCU (V2N family's GD32G553).  Absent on families without one.

ethernet_phy_count.description: Number of populated Ethernet PHY instances.  Only meaningful alongside `ethernet_phy:`; families with a single PHY (or none) omit it.

nor_flash.description: SoC controller / peripheral name that reaches the on-module NOR flash (routing annotation, not a chip slug -- e.g. `xspi`).

nor_flash_driver_status.description: alp-sdk driver maturity for the on-module NOR flash reached via `nor_flash:`. `nor_flash:` names the SoC controller, not a chip slug, so there is no `chips/<part>/` driver to tier -- `none` is the honest (not aspirational) value per ADR 0017 (#1169).

emmc.description: SoC controller / peripheral name that reaches the on-module eMMC (routing annotation -- e.g. `sd0`).

emmc_driver_status.description: alp-sdk driver maturity for the on-module eMMC reached via `emmc:`. `emmc:` names the SoC controller, not a chip slug, so there is no `chips/<part>/` driver to tier -- `none` is the honest (not aspirational) value per ADR 0017 (#1169).

npu.description: Discrete on-module NPU chip (V2M's DEEPX DX-M1).  On-die NPUs (Ethos-U, DRP-AI) are silicon facts and do NOT appear here.

ospi_memories.description: Per-OSPI-instance external memory population (AEN family).  Keys are OSPI controller instances (`ospi0`, `ospi1`).

i2c_devices.description: Per-bus I2C device tables, allowed on every family.  Keys are bus identifiers (e.g. `brd_i2c`, `e1m_i2c0`) consumed by the SDK loader; the key set stays OPEN because bus names are a per-family fact (V2N's `brd_i2c` is a GD32-adjacent Renesas bus, AEN's is the Alif LPI2C0).

memory.description: Off-SoC module memory capacities, REQUIRED on every preset in one canonical shape.  `0` means the SKU populates NONE of that class (e.g. E1M-AEN801, which runs from the SoC's on-die MRAM); `TBD` encodes 'pending the authoritative HW config' or 'per-BOM-variant' (per the no-inventing-values rule).  The two are NOT interchangeable: 0 is a known absence, TBD is an unknown.  On-die SRAM/MRAM is derived from the SoC variant, never declared here.

dram_mbit.description: External volatile memory in Mbit (LPDDR4X on V2N/V2M, HyperRAM on AEN).  0 = none populated on this SKU.

flash_mbit.description: External non-volatile memory in Mbit (eMMC on V2N/V2M, OSPI NOR on AEN).  0 = none populated on this SKU.

inference.description: Inference-accelerator selection.  `preferred_backend` is always required; `ethos_u_variant` (the primary variant) is required whenever the preferred backend is `ethos_u`.  Which Ethos-U variants the part carries is silicon-determined -- derived from the SoC JSON `npus[]` / capability counts -- so the SoM preset does NOT enumerate them (`npu_population` is deprecated, see below).  Non-Ethos backends (drpai, deepx_dxm1) have no per-instance table.

preferred_backend.description: Canonical backend key (`ethos_u`, `drpai`, `deepx_dxm1`, ...).  Cross-checked against the device dispatcher by scripts/check_inference_backend_parity.py.

ethos_u_variant.description: Primary Ethos-U variant (`u55`, `u65`, `u85`) when multiple are populated.

npu_population.description: DEPRECATED — no longer read by the SDK.  Which Ethos-U instances a part carries is silicon-determined and sourced from the SoC JSON `npus[]` (+ the `ethos_u{55,65,85}_count` capabilities); an on-die NPU cannot be depopulated at the SoM level, so restating it here duplicated the SoC.  Retained as an optional field for back-compat with older consumers; do not author it in new presets.  Scheduled for removal in som-preset v2.

capabilities.description: Per-SoM hardware-accelerator / feature capability flags.  DELIBERATELY OPEN keys (values pinned to booleans): the key set is matched against each library's `integration.zephyr.hw_backends:` block in metadata/libraries/<name>.yaml, which grows with the library catalogue -- enumerating it here would couple the preset schema to every library release.  ADDITIVE direction only: declare capabilities the SoM ADDS on top of the silicon (on-module chips, bridge features).  Removing a silicon capability the SKU leaves unpopulated goes in `silicon_capabilities.unpopulated` instead, never as a `false` here.

silicon_capabilities.description: SKU-level RESTRICTION of the referenced silicon's capability set.  A SKU can only remove (mark unpopulated / not-bonded-out) what its SoC JSON `capabilities:` block offers -- never add; additions belong in `capabilities:`.  Optional; when absent the SKU inherits the SoC's full capability set (the default for every current SKU).  Semantic cross-check (scripts/validate_metadata.py): every listed name must resolve to a truthy entry in the referenced SoC JSON's `capabilities:` block and must not also appear in this preset's `capabilities:` block.

unpopulated.description: Capability keys from the SoC JSON `capabilities:` block that this SKU does NOT populate (e.g. an accelerator fused off / not bonded out on this order code).  The loader's resolve_capabilities() forces each listed key to false/0 and scripts/gen_soc_caps.py drops the matching ALP_CAP_* flag for ALP_SOM_<SKU>-gated builds.

topology.description: Per-core default runtime + app mapping.  Keys are canonical `cores[].id` values from the resolved SoC spec (e.g. `a55_cluster`, `m33_sm`, `m55_hp`, `m55_he`, `a32_cluster`, `m33`).  Customer's board.yaml `cores:` block inherits + overrides.  Key set stays open here (it must mirror the SoC's cores[].id set, enforced by the pr-metadata-validate cross-check, not by this schema).

memory_map.description: OPTIONAL declarative memory-region table. Stock SoMs whose memory layout matches the silicon default omit this block; the loader derives effective regions from the SoC JSON variant's `sram_banks_kb` + `mram_mb` (resolved via `silicon_variant`). Declare entries here ONLY for non-stock partitioning (e.g. reserving SRAM for a hardware secure enclave outside the default layout). Per-app IPC carve-outs live in the customer's `board.yaml` `ipc:` block, not here.

mailbox.description: Vendor mailbox / IPC controller + channel reservations.  Required when any topology entry runs Zephyr or baremetal.  Per the project's standing convention, AEN / iMX93 controller name may be TBD until the user supplies the HW-config writeup.

controller.description: Vendor mailbox controller identifier (e.g. `renesas_mhu`, `nxp_mu`, `alif_mhuv2`).  TBD when the hand-written HW config still owes the value.

driver_status.description: alp-sdk driver maturity for the mailbox controller. A directional link (e.g. RX proven, TX unexercised) is a single value short of what this enum can express on its own -- pair it with `notes` when the two directions differ (#1169).

notes.description: Free-form maturity note -- e.g. recording which direction of a bidirectional link is silicon-proven when `driver_status` alone can't capture the split.

pad_routes.description: E1M pads / peripheral instances whose dispatch is worth recording explicitly: routed through a SoM-side mediator chip (e.g., CC3501E coprocessor on AEN, GD32G553 IO MCU on V2N), or -- via `dispatch: unrouted` -- physically open on this revision (reaches neither a mediator nor the main silicon). Pads NOT listed here are assumed to route directly to the main silicon's GPIO / peripheral -- that default is only ever `direct`; a pad that goes nowhere MUST carry an explicit `unrouted` entry rather than falling out of the list silently (#1854). The SDK loader composes this list with the board's `e1m_routes:` block at codegen time: when an E1M pad appears in both blocks, the board supplies the role (e.g., `bmi323_int1`) and the SoM supplies the dispatch path (e.g., CC3501E GPIO 14).

soc_peripheral_instances.description: On-die SoC peripheral instances with pads routed on the module's edge (metadata/e1m_modules/<family>/*.tsv) but no dedicated `on_module:` role -- they are bus/interface instances, not populated parts (no MPN, no chips/*.yaml manifest). Declared here purely so the instance is VISIBLE to the SoM model (a prerequisite for #655's DT/pinctrl generation and for board.yaml requests to bind to) -- this block does NOT itself generate anything and does NOT duplicate the pad list, which stays single-sourced in the TSV. `driver_status: none` is the honest default for an instance with no alp-sdk driver behind it yet; do not mark a tier here that the driver files don't back. `instance` slugs must be unique within a preset -- `uniqueItems` on this array only catches two byte-identical entries, so the real check (same slug, differing class/driver_status) is a semantic cross-check in scripts/validate_metadata.py, not this schema (#1170).

helper_firmware.description: On-module helper MCUs whose firmware images the orchestrator registers into the system manifest.  These are NOT heterogeneous-compute peers (they don't appear in `topology:`).  An entry describes a helper along three INDEPENDENT axes: how it is written locally (`flash_method`/`flash_args`, no preset declares one today), how it is updated in the FIELD (`update_channel`, e.g. AEN's `cc3501e_otp` via `alp_ota_spi_otp` or the GD32 bridge's `alp_ota_spi_bridge`), and WHO may invoke the flash method and when (`flash_policy`).  A helper may declare any combination -- the GD32 bridge carries a field-update channel and a `recovery_only` policy with NO local flash method at all, and AEN's `cc3501e_otp` is the same shape.  See `$defs/helper_firmware_entry`.

preliminary.description: True while the silicon / datasheet the preset encodes is itself preliminary.

partial_hw_config.description: True while any field in the preset is still TBD pending the user-supplied authoritative HW config.

driver_status.description: Shared alp-sdk driver-maturity vocabulary, reused wherever a preset tracks it (`soc_peripheral_instance.driver_status`, `mailbox.driver_status`, `on_module.nor_flash_driver_status`, `on_module.emmc_driver_status`) so the tiers can't drift apart per field. `none` is the honest default absent a matching driver; do not write an aspirational tier (#1169).

oneOf.description: Chip-id slug matching a `metadata/chips/<chip>.yaml` manifest, or an SoC-controller routing annotation (`xspi`, `sd0`).
Part choice pending the user-supplied HW-config writeup / BOM decision.

chip.description: Storage-part MPN (e.g. `MX25UM25645GXDI00`), or the literal `TBD`.  MPN, not a chips/ slug: storage parts have no chip driver.

assembled.description: Population status: true (default), false (DNI), or "optional" (assembled per BOM variant).

interface.description: SoC controller instance the HyperRAM hangs off (e.g. `ospi0`).

assembled.description: Population status: true (default), false (DNI), or "optional" (assembled per BOM variant).  Mirrors ospi_memory.assembled deliberately: without this key the default true silently claimed a HyperRAM on every SKU that merely declared the footprint, which is how E1M-AEN801 came to advertise 256 Mbit of external RAM it does not populate.

variant.description: Ethos-U variant of this instance (`u55`, `u65`, `u85`).  The instance's role/subtype, MAC size, and the host core it pairs with are silicon facts and live once in the SoC JSON (`npus[].subtype` / `mac_per_cycle` / `paired_core`) — a SoM preset does not restate them.

os.description: Default runtime for this core.  Customer's board.yaml `cores.<id>.os` overrides.

app.description: Stock app (`alp-image-edge` for Yocto A-class, `alp-stock-shim` for Zephyr M-class) or a path to a custom app directory.

machine.description: Yocto MACHINE name.  Required for `os: yocto` entries.

board.description: Zephyr board target name.  Required for `os: zephyr` entries.

hw_console.description: False when this core has no hardware UART console (headless -- e.g. the RZ/V2N M33 system-manager, whose debug UART the A55 owns).  Absent defaults to true.  A SoM-topology fact, not customer-overridable in board.yaml; consumed by `diagnostics.sim_console:` to stream the RAM console over the studio simulator's `uart_socket` (issue #686).

zephyr_full_name.description: Human-readable board title for `os: zephyr` entries -- feeds `--emit zephyr-board`'s generated `board.yml` `full_name:`, the twister board `.yaml` `name:` (families that reuse it verbatim), and the board `.dts` header comment / `model =` property (parenthetical stripped). Free text so it stays a literal, reviewable fact rather than a string built by regex over other fields.

zephyr_twister_name.description: Twister board-metadata `name:` field for `os: zephyr` entries, when it differs from `zephyr_full_name` (some families drop the SoC parenthetical here). Defaults to `zephyr_full_name` when absent.

base.description: Physical base address.  TBD when the hand-written HW config still owes the value.

size_mib.description: Region size in MiB.  Provide either size_mib or size_kib.

size_kib.description: Region size in KiB.  Provide either size_mib or size_kib.

accessible_from.description: Core IDs that can access the region.  Must match keys in `topology:`.

cacheable.description: When true the region is cacheable from all `accessible_from` cores.  Default carve-out is non-cacheable.

carveout.description: LEGACY OVERRIDE (#1365 split B) that MUST AGREE with the region's DERIVED class where one is resolvable; it is no longer the primary signal.  `scripts/alp_orchestrate/carveout.py` (IPC carve-out eligibility) and `scripts/alp_orchestrate/partition.py` (flash-device eligibility) now derive a region's class against the SoC's declared on-die MRAM aperture (`scripts/alp_orchestrate/aperture.py`) -- a region CONTAINED in the aperture is flash-class regardless of this flag.  This field is honoured VERBATIM only as a fallback: where the SoC declares no aperture at all (every non-Alif SoM), or this region's own `base` is unresolved (e.g. `mram_main`'s `"TBD"`), there is nothing to derive a class from, so the authored value here decides -- and it decides BEFORE `write_authority:` in that fallback: when a region's base is unresolved and BOTH fields are authored, `carveout:` wins (the conservative, pre-split-B signal) and `write_authority:` is consulted only when this field is absent.  Historically (pre-split-B): when explicitly false, the region was excluded from IPC carve-out allocation and from `_known_flash_devices()`/`storage[].flash_device:` (#1484) even though it declares a real `base` -- for a flash-class region (e.g. an MRAM MCUboot/slot0/reserved/storage sub-region that must publish a base so the board generator can lay out its partition table) that base is NOT byte-addressable shared memory a raw_shmem/rpmsg carve-out can safely land in.  Defaults to true (eligible).  NOT deprecated or removed -- `additionalProperties: false` would break every existing `carveout: false` row and any customer copy -- but a value that DISAGREES with a resolvable derived class is a metadata bug to fix, not a silently-honoured override.

write_authority.description: WHO may write this region, and WHEN.  Modelled on `helper_firmware_entry.flash_policy`, and deliberately two-axis: a one-axis customer/vendor/secure split collapses `he_slot0` onto `storage` (both customer) and cannot separate flash-time from runtime, which is the distinction the hazard needs.  `customer_image` = written only by the flash tool, never by running code (`he_slot0`, `hp_slot0`).  `vendor_image` = a factory-provisioned image (`mcuboot`).  `customer_runtime` = runtime-writable by the application, and the ONLY value an IPC carve-out or a runtime mount may ever land on (`storage`).  `secure_enclave` = written by the Secure Enclave at provisioning (`atoc`); the SE is not a `topology:` core, so it can never appear in `accessible_from` and no core id can express this.  `none` = nobody writes it (`reserved` headroom) -- an explicit no-writer, not a catch-all.  `composite` = a whole-device alias spanning contained rows of DIFFERENT authority (`mram_main`), where a single value would be false by construction; consult the contained rows.  ABSENT MEANS UNRESOLVED, NEVER `customer_runtime` -- a consumer must treat an authored region carrying no `write_authority` as ineligible for both IPC carve-out and runtime write, and say so, rather than defaulting permissively (ADR-0034 clause 4).  Not in `required` for som-preset v1 because `docs/porting-new-som.md` is a public porting guide and a customer preset that authored `memory_map:` rows would break at `tan validate` on upgrade; `scripts/validate_metadata.py` enforces presence semantically instead, and v2 promotes it.  NOTE `accessible_from:` is read/execute reachability only and says nothing about write authority: `atoc` lists `[m55_he, m55_hp]` and neither may write it (#1365).
write_authority.$comment: ADR-0027's role->region mapping must consume this field rather than growing a parallel flag: a `role:` may only resolve onto a `customer_runtime` region.

access_windows.description: OPTIONAL per-core addressable sub-window of this region, keyed by core id.  `accessible_from:` is a yes/no per core and cannot express "this core reaches only PART of the region" -- the RZ/V2N Cortex-M33 does exactly that (FSP bsp_slave_address.h: CM33-secure 0x80000000 / CM33-non-secure 0x90000000 -> A55 0x40000000, 256 MiB) while ddr_main spans 4 GiB.  Declare the reachable slice here and scripts/alp_orchestrate/carveout.py confines that core's IPC carve-outs to it instead of allocating at the region top, where the address does not exist for that core.  Omit for regions every accessible_from core reaches in full.

base.description: Window base in the SAME address space as the region's own `base` (i.e. the physical/host view), NOT the aliased address the core issues.

note.description: Provenance for the window -- name the vendor header/manual it was read from.

dt_label.description: Optional Zephyr Devicetree label for this region.  Used by the storage emitter when board.yaml `storage:` entries reference this region as their `flash_device:`; the emitted overlay decorates `&<dt_label>` with a `partitions { ... }` child node.  Defaults to the region `name` when omitted, which is only safe when the region name already IS its Devicetree label -- verify against the generated board `.dts` before relying on the default (AEN's `mram_main`, for example, names its flash node `mram_storage`, not `mram_main`).  Since alp-sdk#1556, `resolve_storage_partitions()` enforces this itself: a `storage:` entry cannot reach `status: ok` on a region that omits this field, so an unverified default now blocks with a reason instead of silently resolving.  A region with `carveout: false` is a partition INSIDE a flash-class node, not a flash device of its own, and is refused as a `flash_device:` target regardless of this field (#1484).

name.description: Helper-MCU instance identifier (e.g. `gd32_bridge`, `cc3501e_otp`).  Unique within the SoM preset's helper_firmware list.

firmware_path.description: Repo-relative path to the prebuilt / shipped firmware image.  Omit this key entirely when no artefact exists yet (schema-legal -- only `name`, `chip` and `flash_policy` are required).

flash_method.description: Backend tool key naming the transport by which this helper's image is WRITTEN locally.  TBD pending the authoritative flow.  Independent of `update_channel` (which answers how the device is updated in the FIELD): an entry may carry both.  It says nothing about who is allowed to invoke it -- that is `flash_policy`, which is REQUIRED on every helper entry regardless of which of these two keys it carries.  NO SoM preset declares this key today: `swd_probe` was removed from the four E1M-X GD32 bridge entries when GD32 programming was separated out of `tan` (#1439, tan-cli#732).

flash_args.description: Backend-specific args (interface, target, base address, ...) forwarded verbatim to the flash backend.  DELIBERATELY OPEN object: the shape follows `flash_method`'s backend contract, which this schema cannot enumerate; TBD when the method is TBD.  Only meaningful alongside `flash_method`.

flash_policy.description: WHO may invoke `flash_method`, and WHEN.  REQUIRED on every helper entry -- there is no absent-means-`customer` default; a helper with no local flash path at all (no `flash_method`) still states who may reach it if one is ever added.  `customer`: a genuine customer flash target.  `factory`: programmed by Alp Lab in production, never a customer flash target.  `recovery_only`: programmed by Alp Lab in production, and customer-flashable ONLY to recover a bricked device, with Alp Lab-supplied binaries.  Independent of `update_channel`, which answers how the device is updated in the FIELD -- a helper can carry both, and the GD32 bridge does.

update_channel.description: How this helper's firmware is updated in the FIELD, once the module is in a customer's hands.  `alp_ota_spi_otp` (AEN's `cc3501e_otp`): Alp-released firmware applied over the bridge SPI link, programming the chip's own OTP.  `alp_ota_spi_bridge` (the GD32 bridge): streamed over the bridge link into a slot-A/B application bootloader with commit + rollback -- a DIFFERENT value on purpose, because the GD32 has no OTP to program.  Independent of `flash_method`; declaring a channel does not by itself make the helper un-flashable, and does not imply anything about who may flash it -- that is `flash_policy`.

instance.description: Instance slug local to this SoM, e.g. `riic1`, `i3c30`, `rspi0`, `canfd2`.

class.description: Peripheral class, matching a `metadata/socs/**.json` `peripherals:` key family (e.g. `i2c`, `i3c`, `spi`, `pdm`, `can`, `uart`, `i2s`).

silicon_peripheral.description: The pad-route source's `silicon_peripheral` name/prefix this instance corresponds to (e.g. `RIIC1_`), for traceability back to metadata/e1m_modules/<family>/*.tsv.

driver_status.description: alp-sdk driver maturity for this instance. `none` (the default assumption) is the honest value while no zephyr/drivers/** node targets it -- do not write an aspirational tier.

e1m.description: E1M-standard pad or peripheral instance identifier, e.g. `E1M_GPIO_IO15`, `E1M_SPI1`, `E1M_PWM0`.

dispatch.description: SoM-side mediator the pad routes through. `direct` is the default for pads not in the list; an explicit `direct` entry is allowed for clarity. `unrouted` marks a pad that is physically open on this hardware revision -- it reaches neither a mediator nor the main silicon's GPIO / peripheral -- and MUST be listed here explicitly; there is no implicit `unrouted` default (an absent entry always means `direct`). The SDK's GPIO dispatch path refuses to open an `unrouted` pad with ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT instead of silently driving a pin that goes nowhere (#1854). `TBD` marks pads whose routing is pending the user's HW-config writeup (per the no-inventing-values rule).

dispatch_pin.description: Mediator-local pin or bus identifier. Forms: integer (CC3501E GPIO index, e.g. `14`); single pad name (`"PA11"` for a GD32 port pad); bus pin (`"SPI1.MISO"`); or a slash-joined pair for multi-pin peripherals (`"PA0/PB3"` for a quadrature encoder's X/Y pads). Meaningless for `dispatch: unrouted` (there is no mediator pin to name); omit it there.

doc.description: One-line free-form note (matches the e1m_routes entry shape on the board side). Required for `dispatch: unrouted` -- the whole point of that state is to record WHY the pad is dead (e.g. which revision/pin it moved from).

bus_master.description: Which silicon drives the bus (informational).  Omitted when no on-module silicon masters the bus (e.g. AEN's slave-only LPI2C0 housekeeping bus, ADR 0017).

role.description: Role this chip plays on the bus, e.g. `pmic_main_page0`, `rtc`, `temp_sensor`.

oneOf.description: 7-bit I2C address as a hex string, e.g. "0x50".
Address pending the user-supplied HW-config writeup.
Address picked by the chip's firmware (e.g. GD32 supervisor MCU) -- not a hardware-fixed value.

assembled.description: Population status: true (default), false (DNI), or "optional" (assembled per BOM variant).

notes.description: Free-form note (rare in the public form -- design rationale belongs in the private metadata repo).

broadcast_address.description: True when `address_7bit` is a broadcast / global-call address multiple devices on this bus legitimately answer BY DESIGN (e.g. the TAS2563 family's 0x48 global-call write-only address, metadata/chips/tas2563.yaml). Excludes this entry from scripts/validate_metadata.py's duplicate-(bus,address_7bit) collision check (#1845). Do NOT set this to silence a real strap conflict between two unrelated devices -- document a real conflict via `notes:` instead and fix the strap.
